research_rationale:
Executive Order 13624 (August 30, 2012; 77 FR 54779) directs the Departments of Energy, Commerce and Agriculture and the Environmental Protection Agency, in coordination with named White House offices, to coordinate policies to encourage investment in industrial energy efficiency and combined heat and power (CHP), to engage stakeholders, and to take the listed supporting actions. The held Federal Register original was read in full. It has no sunset, expiry, termination condition or revocation; its only dates are the policy goal date of the end of 2020 in Sec. 2(a) and a 25 percent energy-intensity goal over 10 years, which describes an existing Department of Energy program in Sec. 2(c)(iv), not a limit on the order. The United States Code (release point 119-121, printed through 2026-10-09) prints the order in full as a note under 42 U.S.C. 6341 with no ending statement. A Department of Energy notice signed January 5, 2026 (91 FR 704, FR Doc. 2026-00153) still cites Executive Order 13624 as statutory authority for an information collection, which shows agency reliance but is not itself a legal predicate. The search of the held corpus for the order's number found only the order's own text and that notice, so no held later order amends, revokes or supersedes it; the Federal Register catalog note is empty, which does not establish current effect. The YES rests on the order's terms, the Code note and the absence of any held ending instrument.
